items.title: Sudhalter interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2019
items.q: I don't remember what it was, either Mozart or Beethoven or something straight through.

ctx.x: Like I’m thinking to myself well do I try to get this person more hip to the chords and the note choices or should I just don’t mess with it.

Yeah, you don’t know what your role is, I know. Well I have three students right now who are super interesting, and one is exactly like that. He’s a kid that — I mean he doesn’t really know if I put a piece in front of him is this in the category of classical or jazz. He doesn’t know anything about terms or theory. He can just barely know what key he is in or something. But when I put on a blues on the speaker with an iReal background, or a “Watermelon Man” or whatever, you know, he will just make the most…

try to get him to understand what the notes of the chords are you know. At the most I might just show him a blues scale or something like that, and just point out that he is already using those notes you know. But just to help him know the name of what it is. But yeah, it’s a very very delicate question. And years ago I had a very deep experience in that category. Not so much with the improvising but with messing with what’s already been happening. A gentleman brought me his son, who was probably about seven or…
